memos.risk:
Ticket size: $5 minimum, not $20. Pool depth is 85.8 SOL (~$15k-ish at these prices), so a $20 ticket plus a 1.4-5.1% round trip is a meaningful slice of available liquidity and likely pays heavy impact.

Stop: 30% from entry. The coin already sits 32% below its 30-minute high, so a tight stop may trigger immediately; if the desk buys, use 25-30% and accept the noise.

Hold: 15-30 minutes max. Post-graduation buyers have been net sellers in the first two minutes (sell/buy 0.94), and the 15-minute window shows net outflow of 30.5 SOL, so momentum is not on our side.

Refuse if: the coin is classed as anything other than ORGANIC, the bundle share (46%) is treated as a warning sign, or the desk cannot accept a near-break-even outcome. Honestly, bundling near 46% plus a launch bot and sell pressure argue for skipping. My recommendation is pass unless the desk has a specific reason to take a $5 lottery ticket.
memos.scout:
The strongest honest case is the flow. Over the last 15 minutes, buyers outnumbered sellers (279 vs 189), buy volume was $29.4k, and net flow was positive at +30.5 SOL, with the price up 17% in that window. Buyers stayed active through the drawdown, and the top three holders control only 8.4% of the curve, with the top five first-2-minute buyers at 21%. That is not a single operator dumping.

But the brief undercuts most of it. The buyer count is inflated by a 46% bundle share and a 42% completer share, which suggests coordinated or bot-driven buying rather than broad organic demand. Post-graduation sell-to-buy was 0.94 and a launch bot was present. The coin is 32% off its 30-minute high, the 30-minute return is roughly flat, and the pool is thin at 86 SOL, so a $20 round trip faces meaningful slippage. The current classification is ORGANIC, yet the bundle share is high enough to question that label.

My verdict: there is a real short-term flow case, but not a convincing one for 30-60 minutes out. Given the base rates for alive coins in this age window, I would skip unless the bundle share and launch-bot signals were clearly absent, which they are not.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: the 32% drawdown from the 30-minute high, with a shallow 85.8 SOL pool, means a sell-off can cut deeper than the fees. The bundle share of 45.8% and completer share of 41.5% point to coordinated early wallets that may distribute into any bounce. Last 15 minutes show sell SOL (105.5) at 78% of buy SOL (136.1), with 189 sellers against 279 buyers, so net flow of +30.5 SOL is thin support. Launch bot present and sell-to-buy of 0.94 in the first two minutes suggest early flippers. A 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost is small against a 32% drawdown, but a reversal back through the high is not supported by the data. Skip.
